## Code review: WA-3438 network picker (2 commits)

I ran a shortened version of the review. The diff is 27 lines across 2 files, so I read it myself instead of starting the nine category agents and the validate/refute agents. No findings were independently checked by those agents, so **there's no score**. You can treat the verdict as solid for a change this small.

**Scope:** 2 files, +22 −5 · base `725dbf4` → `6e8e123` (committed only)
- `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/AddAccounts/AddManually.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/AddAccounts/__tests__/AddManually.test.tsx`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Ready to open the PR |
| **Blocking (P0–P1)** | None |
| **Worth fixing (P2)** | None |
| **Minor (P3)** | 1, in testing |

### What I checked, and why none of it is a problem

- **Closed network picker label** (`AddManually.tsx:115`): the trigger now draws its label with `ChainIndicator`. Before this change it showed the raw chain ID (`"1"`), which is the bug the component library's own note warns about (`components/ui/select.tsx:38-40`). `NetworkSelector` (`components/common/NetworkSelector/index.tsx:365`) and `MemberInfoForm.tsx:51` do the same thing.
  - The value is never empty: it defaults to `chains.eth` and `onValueChange` ignores null (line 110). So `ChainIndicator` never falls back to the chain from the URL.
  - A chain that isn't in `configs` now shows "Unknown network" instead of a bare number, which is better.
  - `value` comes in typed as `any` from base-ui (`SelectValue.d.ts:30`), but that's the library's type, not new code writing `any`.
- **Bottom alignment** (`AddManually.tsx:97`): I worried that with `md:items-end`, a validation error under the address field would push the picker out of line. It doesn't. `AddressInput` shows its error in the label above the field (`AddressInput/index.tsx:181, 214`) and renders nothing below it, so the bottoms stay lined up. On mobile the layout is unchanged because the class only applies from `md` up.
- **Test setup** (`AddManually.test.tsx:8-15`): the `jest.mock` factory now uses the module-level `chainConfigs`. That's fine: `next/jest` uses SWC, which doesn't enforce babel's `mock` prefix rule, and the variable is only read when the component renders.
- **The new test fails if the fix is removed.** Without the render function the trigger shows `"1"`, which doesn't contain `"Chain 1"`. The item list renders in a portal outside `network-selector`, so it can't make the assertion pass by accident.
- **Security, performance, regression, architecture, reuse:** nothing to report. There's no new data flow, no new calls, nothing exported changes, and it follows the repo's existing pattern.

### Findings

| # | Priority | Area | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P3 | testing | `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/AddAccounts/__tests__/AddManually.test.tsx:58` | The test only covers the default chain (Ethereum). Nothing checks that the closed trigger updates after the user picks another network, even though Polygon (`137`) is already in the test data. If a later change hard-coded `chains.eth` in the render function, or dropped `value={chainId}`, this test would still pass. **Fix:** add a case that opens the select, picks `137`, and expects `network-selector` to contain `Chain 137`. |

### Worth tidying
Nothing proposed. The touched files already follow the repo's patterns.

### Not covered
- I didn't run the tests, type-check or lint, as you asked.
- I didn't check the layout visually. The alignment conclusion comes from reading the code, not a screenshot.
- The findings weren't checked by the paired validate/refute agents, and no score was produced.

Also, several connected services (Slack, Gmail, Google Drive and others) need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings before they'll work. This review didn't need any of them.
